claim: A law called The Flora and Fauna Act classified aboriginal people as animals until Australian voters overturned it in the 1960s.
justification: No Australian federal or state legislation officially titled "The Flora and Fauna Act" has ever existed, and no Australian law ever explicitly classified Aboriginal Australians as "flora" or "fauna." The 1967 referendum amended the Constitution to allow the Commonwealth to make laws for Aboriginal people (Section 51(xxvi)) and to include them in population counts (repealing Section 127), but it did not repeal or modify any act by that name ([University of Queensland](https://web.library.uq.edu.au/blog/2017/05/1967-referendum)). The myth is believed to have originated as a rhetorical statement within the Aboriginal activist movement in the 1970s, with scholar Marcia Langton calling it a "joke" first used by Lester or Jerry Bostock at a FCAATSI conference in 1977 ([Club Troppo](https://clubtroppo.com.au/2013/06/03/were-indigenous-people-regulated-by-the-flora-fauna-act/)). It gained traction through conflation with the well-documented history of racist Australian legislation, but no legislative record, statute book, or archival document supports its existence ([SBS](https://www.sbs.com.au/nitv/article/shareena-clanton-is-like-many-of-us-a-victim-of-the-flora-and-fauna-act-myth/m40dgtgah)).

The evidence explicitly states this is a persistent myth, with no legal text ever classifying Aboriginal Australians as "flora" or "fauna." The 1967 referendum, while historically significant for amending the Constitution to recognize Aboriginal people in census counts and allow federal legislation for them, did not repeal or modify any such act, as it simply did not exist.

The evidence is clear and comprehensive, leaving no gaps requiring further investigation. Both sources consistently reject the claim's factual basis, and no conflicting information exists within the record on the core issue of the act's existence or the nature of the 1967 referendum.

Therefore, the claim is not supported by the fact-check findings. The knowledge explicitly and clearly refutes it.
